question: When `subagent_runs` is empty, `runs.json` remains, and no durable receipt proves which state is authoritative, should automatic migration preserve-and-warn or import the legacy records under a narrower provenance rule?
rationale: Both choices can undermine user trust differently: automatic import can resurrect stale runs, while preservation without import can hide legitimate upgrade state and require operator intervention; repository history cannot determine the intended product contract.

options.title: Preserve, warn, and add resolution
options.body: Keep the fail-safe non-import default and expose a supported doctor or CLI action to inspect and explicitly import or discard the ambiguous source.

options.title: Accept warning-only preservation
options.body: Land the current preserve-and-warn behavior and intentionally require manual operator recovery outside the normal product flow.

options.title: Import with narrow provenance
options.body: Automatically import only when table and database provenance proves the legacy source predates canonical subagent ownership, with upgrade tests for each allowed case.

recommendation.title: Preserve, warn, and add resolution
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-safe non-import default and expose a supported doctor or CLI action to inspect and explicitly import or discard the ambiguous source.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent adjacent SQLite migration and recovery history makes this the strongest available owner for the upgrade-safety choice.
